summary: During this verification run, Xiara died five times to what appears to be the same unfightable 'Crazed Dragonhawk' (entry 15650, faction template 7) documented in docs/evidence/m2/README.md's 'A creature that kills the character but cannot be fought' section.
evidenceForCause: tuicraft fight <Crazed Dragonhawk guid> was refused with unverified_hostile_relation in the M2 evidence run, so it cannot be fought or fled from tactically.

Every death in this session happened while Xiara was standing still or slowly probing movement/ground-refusal directions in the x~8734-8755, y~-6524..-6580 band where 1-2 Crazed Dragonhawks were consistently observed roaming (confirmed via nearby --all --json with distances recomputed from the live predicted pose, since the tool's own reported 'distance' field is computed from a stale serverPose).

Health loss in this band was fast (multiple hundred-HP-equivalent chip damage in 1-4 seconds) and NOT correlated with the intended Springpaw Stalker target's health, which stayed at its starting value during several of the fatal windows.
Health never dropped once Xiara was moved more than roughly 60-100 yards away from that x/y band, and regenerated normally to full at a safe distance every time.

deathLog.context: Idle near (8721-8745, -6558..-6572) while doing lease/ground-refusal CLI tests after the first corpse reclaim
Within ~2s of the second corpse reclaim, before any player action other than a Renew self-cast
During approach toward a Springpaw Stalker for the second (kiting) encounter, before combat began
During the fast approach + movement/cast test near the same stalker
Immediately after a second movement/cast test attempt and a delayed flee

mitigationThatWorked: Reclaiming the corpse and immediately issuing face+move away (no intervening cast/check) toward the graveyard, without pausing in the hazard band, reliably escaped with no further damage and full natural regen within ~15 seconds.
relationToExitEvidenceItem6: This is itself part of the item 6 finding: in a world with an unfightable, aggressive wandering mob nearby, time spent idle or slow-probing while verifying movement primitives is dangerous independent of the tactical movement system under test, and a Jev-driven kiting choice that runs the character further into open ground for many consecutive decisions (see encounter-02-kite-blocked.json) has no situational awareness of that hazard. Movement helped survival once in this session (the deliberate post-reclaim flee); it played no defensive role during the four other deaths because the hazard was never in the offered candidate set.
